subject.title: Feature request: config option to suppress transient tool error warnings

question: Should OpenClaw add a public success-aware tool-error delivery policy for normal chat surfaces, and if so what exact modes should it expose?
rationale: The remaining work changes user-visible failure safety and adds config surface; source inspection shows a narrow implementation path, but the safe product contract is not deterministic from code alone.

options.title: Add opt-in policy
options.body: Expose a default-safe `messages.toolErrorDelivery` style policy with current behavior as default, plus explicit `final` and/or `off` modes backed by tests and docs.

options.title: Keep current boolean
options.body: Treat `messages.suppressToolErrors` plus channel-specific suppression as sufficient and close or narrow this issue after maintainer confirmation.

options.title: Channel-specific controls
options.body: Route this to per-channel/operator policy instead of a core global config, accepting more setup complexity for finer safety boundaries.

recommendation.title: Add opt-in policy
recommendation.body: Expose a default-safe `messages.toolErrorDelivery` style policy with current behavior as default, plus explicit `final` and/or `off` modes backed by tests and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: They most recently owned the current warning-policy and Telegram suppression behavior and merged the prior narrow fix that left this issue open.
